last_transition_reason: The proof correctly establishes that n is odd and gcd(n,2d)=1 from n ≡ 1 mod 2d, then shows U_{d,n}(ζ) ≠ 0 for every nontrivial nth root of unity ζ by contradiction from ζ^{dj} = -1 and oddness of n. The coprimality argument with M_n(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2 is complete: any nonconstant common divisor would yield a complex root α that is either a nontrivial nth root coming from [n]_q(α)=0 or a primitive nth root coming from Φ_n(α)=0, contradicting the established nonvanishing of U_{d,n} at all such α. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used.
latest_nl_proof:
Only the congruence n ≡ 1 mod 2d is needed in the argument below; the hypotheses involving r are harmless but not used.

Because n ≡ 1 mod 2d, there is an integer t with n = 1 + 2dt. Hence n is odd. Also, if g is any common divisor of n and 2d, then g divides 2dt = n - 1 as well, so g divides n - (n - 1) = 1. Therefore gcd(n,2d) = 1.

Now let ζ be any complex number with ζ^n = 1 and ζ ≠ 1. Suppose, for contradiction, that U_{d,n}(ζ) = 0. Since
U_{d,n}(ζ) = ∏_{j=1}^{n-1} (1 + ζ^{dj}),
there must exist some j with 1 ≤ j ≤ n - 1 such that 1 + ζ^{dj} = 0. Thus ζ^{dj} = -1. Raising both sides to the nth power gives
1 = (ζ^{dj})^n = (-1)^n = -1,
because n is odd. This is impossible. Hence every factor 1 + ζ^{dj} is nonzero, and therefore U_{d,n}(ζ) ≠ 0.

It remains to prove gcd(U_{d,n}(q), M_n(q)) = 1 in Z[q]. Suppose instead that there exists a nonconstant common divisor H(q) ∈ Z[q] of U_{d,n}(q) and M_n(q). Viewing H as a polynomial in C[q], it is still nonconstant, so by the fundamental theorem of algebra it has some complex root α. Then H(α) = 0. Since H divides M_n(q) = [n]_q Φ_n(q)^2, we have M_n(α) = 0, so either [n]_q evaluated at q = α is 0, or Φ_n(α) = 0.

If [n]_q evaluated at q = α is 0, then using the geometric-sum identity [n]_q = 1 + q + ··· + q^{n-1}, we get [n]_1 = n ≠ 0, so α ≠ 1. Also,
(α - 1)[n]_q|_{q=α} = α^n - 1,
so α^n - 1 = 0. Thus α^n = 1 and α ≠ 1.

If Φ_n(α) = 0, then by the defining property of the nth cyclotomic polynomial, α is a primitive nth root of unity. In particular α^n = 1 and α ≠ 1.

So in either case α is a nontrivial nth root of unity. By the previous paragraph, U_{d,n}(α) ≠ 0. But H divides U_{d,n}, and H(α) = 0, so necessarily U_{d,n}(α) = 0, a contradiction.

Therefore U_{d,n}(q) and M_n(q) have no nonconstant common divisor in Z[q]. Equivalently, gcd(U_{d,n}(q), M_n(q)) = 1 in Z[q].
role_in_parent: Shows that the clearing factor U_{d,n}(q) is invertible modulo the final modulus in the localization.
statement_nl: Let [m]_q=(1-q^m)/(1-q), let Φ_n(q) be the nth cyclotomic polynomial, define M_n(q):=[n]_q Φ_n(q)^2, and define U_{d,n}(q):=∏_{j=1}^{n-1}(1+q^{dj}). Suppose d and r are positive integers with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and suppose n>1 satisfies n ≡ 1 mod 2d. Then n is odd and gcd(n,2d)=1. Consequently, if ζ is any complex number with ζ^n=1 and ζ ≠ 1, then U_{d,n}(ζ) ≠ 0. In particular gcd(U_{d,n}(q),M_n(q))=1 in Z[q].

domain_restrictions: d and r are positive integers.
n is an integer greater than 1.
The congruence condition is with respect to 2d.
The q-integer [m]_q is treated as a polynomial expression in the formal variable q.
zeta must satisfy zeta^n = 1 and zeta != 1.
The gcd statement is in the polynomial ring Z[q].
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r) = 1 and r <= d, and for all integers n greater than 1 satisfying n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the integer n is odd and coprime to 2d. For every complex nth root of unity zeta different from 1, the value of U_{d,n} at zeta is nonzero. Therefore U_{d,n}(q) and M_n(q) have no nonconstant common divisor in Z[q].
quantifier_order: For each positive integers d and r, assume gcd(d,r) = 1 and r <= d.
For each positive integer n greater than 1, assume n is congruent to 1 modulo 2d.
Under those assumptions, conclude that n is odd and gcd(n, 2d) = 1.
For every complex number zeta satisfying zeta^n = 1 and zeta != 1, conclude that U_{d,n}(zeta) is nonzero.
Equivalently, the polynomials U_{d,n}(q) and M_n(q) are coprime in Z[q].

The nonvanishing claim for U_{d,n}(zeta) depends on the fixed parameters d and n, not on a separately chosen witness.
